mainTopic: The traveler's pouch on שבת: חרש or קטן, the hidden method of carrying less than four אמות, the eighteen גזירות, putting the pouch on a donkey, and liability for מחמר
overview: The amud continues the משנה about a traveler whose money pouch is with him when שבת begins. First the גמרא asks whether the pouch should go to a חרש or a קטן. According to רבי אליעזר it goes to the קטן, since a חרש may have some understanding. According to the רבנן the two are equal, and two traditions are recorded without a decision. If nobody at all is available, רבי יצחק reveals a method the חכמים kept hidden: carry it less than four אמות at a time. They hid it so people would not slip into carrying a full four אמות in a רשות הרבים. A ברייתא then records רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע disagreeing over whether the eighteen גזירות strengthened the תורה or overloaded the people, each with a parable. Back to the משנה: placing the pouch on a donkey seems to be the forbidden act of מחמר. רב אדא בר אהבה answers that the pouch is put on and taken off only while the donkey walks. רב פפא then explains why a donkey is allowed but a fellow Jew is not. רב אדא בר אהבה also rules that a person may run home with a package already on his shoulder. Finally, רמי בר חמא says מחמר brings חטאת or סקילה, and רבא offers two refutations. The second refutation is pushed aside, while the first, a comparison to עבודה זרה, stands.

steps.title: End of the source: a חרש's תרומה stays in doubt
steps.stepSummary: The quoted source ends: the תרומה of a חרש does not go back to being חולין, because his status is a ספק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It does not go out to become regular (non-holy) food, because he is a doubtful case.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the source the גמרא was quoting on the previous amud. It shows that according to רבי אליעזר, a חרש is treated as possibly having real understanding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תרומה of a חרש were simply invalid, the food would stay regular חולין. Because it stays in a doubtful holy status, we learn that רבי אליעזר treats the חרש as possibly having דעת. So for him, a חרש is 'more grown-up' than a קטן, and the pouch should go to the קטן.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute, treated in הלכה as lacking full understanding

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the tail end of a source that began earlier, quoted to resolve the question according to רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: it does not go out to non-sacred status,
phrases.notes: Speaking of the תרומה separated by a חרש.

phrases.english: because he is a doubtful case.
phrases.notes: His level of understanding is uncertain.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא תֵּצֵא לְחוּלִּין, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא סָפֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the source cited on the previous amud that resolves the dilemma according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.raayaObject: According to רבי אליעזר, a חרש has more understanding than a קטן, so the pouch goes to the קטן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's ruling that a חרש's תרומה remains in doubt and does not revert to חולין.

steps.title: The question really applies according to the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the dilemma only exists according to the רבנן. They list a חרש and a קטן together as people whose תרומה is invalid, so the two are equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: When you ask this question, ask it according to the רבנן. As we learned: five kinds of people may not separate תרומה, and if they did, it is not תרומה. They are: a חרש, a שוטה, and a קטן; one who separates תרומה from produce that is not his; and a גוי who separated תרומה from a Jew's produce, even with permission. His תרומה is not תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves the question away from רבי אליעזר, for whom it is already answered, to the רבנן. It quotes a משנה showing that the רבנן treat a חרש and a קטן exactly the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the תרומה of a חרש is fully invalid, just like the תרומה of a קטן. Since neither has legal understanding, nothing about their status decides between them. That is why the question can be asked at all.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the opinion of the Rabbis
As we learned in a משנה
The portion of produce given to a כהן
A person who is mentally incompetent

phrases.english: When you raise this question, it is according to the Rabbis,
as we learned: five may not separate teruma,
and if they separated, their teruma is not teruma,
these are they: a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor,
phrases.notes: The deaf-mute and the minor are listed side by side.

phrases.english: and one who separates teruma from what is not his,
and a non-Jew who separated teruma from a Jew's produce
even with his permission, his teruma is not teruma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the question is solved for רבי אליעזר, the גמרא narrows it to the רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the question to one opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dilemma applies according to everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: It applies only according to the רבנן, who treat a חרש and a קטן as equal.

steps.title: Deaf-mute or minor: two competing reasons
steps.stepSummary: Should the pouch go to the חרש, because the קטן will one day grow up? Or to the קטן, because people might mistake the חרש for a normal adult?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law? Does he give it to the deaf-mute, because the minor will reach understanding? Or perhaps he gives it to the minor, because the deaf-mute may be mistaken for a healthy adult?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the actual question and gives one reason for each choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חרש: a קטן will grow into a full adult who keeps the מצוות, so we should not train him to carry on שבת. For the קטן: a חרש looks like a grown man, so onlookers might think it is permitted to hand a pouch to an adult. A child is clearly not obligated, so nobody would be misled.

keyTerms.meaning: Will reach the stage of understanding (grow up)
To be mistaken for or confused with

phrases.english: What is the law?
Does he give it to the deaf-mute,
because the minor will come to the stage of understanding,
or perhaps he gives it to the minor,
because the deaf-mute may be mistaken for a competent adult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the dilemma now that it has been placed according to the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which is preferable to carry the pouch on שבת, a חרש or a קטן?

steps.title: Two traditions, no final decision
steps.stepSummary: Some say it goes to the חרש and some say it goes to the קטן. The question is left with two versions.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say he gives it to the deaf-mute; some say he gives it to the minor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports two different traditions about the answer and does not decide between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each tradition follows one of the two reasons from the question. There is no single ruling here. The גמרא simply records both views.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say; there is a version that says

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר the pouch goes to the קטן. According to the רבנן, the חרש and the קטן are equal, and there are two traditions with no final decision.

phrases.english: Some say he gives it to the deaf-mute,
some say he gives it to the minor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma with two competing traditions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two versions: one says give it to the חרש, the other says give it to the קטן.

steps.title: What if nobody is available at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what a person should do if there is no גוי, no donkey, no חרש, no שוטה, and no קטן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is no non-Jew, no donkey, no deaf-mute, no imbecile, and no minor there, what should he do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the worst case, where every option from the משנה and the previous discussion is missing. This sets up רבי יצחק's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every solution so far needed someone or something else to carry the pouch. Now the traveler is completely alone with his money. The question is whether he has any permitted way to keep it.

keyTerms.meaning: There is not there; none are present

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שָׁם לֹא גּוֹי וְלֹא חֲמוֹר
phrases.english: If there is neither a non-Jew nor a donkey

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא חֵרֵשׁ וְלֹא שׁוֹטֶה וְלֹא קָטָן,
phrases.english: nor a deaf-mute nor an imbecile nor a minor,
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין שָׁם לֹא גּוֹי וְלֹא חֲמוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the חרש versus קטן question to the case where no carrier exists at all.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What a traveler alone should do with his pouch when שבת begins.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: there was a hidden method
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says there was another method, but the חכמים did not want to reveal it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: There was yet another method, and the חכמים did not want to reveal it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers that a solution exists but was kept secret. This creates two follow-up questions: what the method is, and why it was hidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is short on purpose. It tells us a solution exists without saying what it is. The next steps explain both the method and the reason for hiding it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
There was yet another option,
and the Sages did not want to reveal it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: עוֹד אַחֶרֶת הָיְתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what to do when nobody is available.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is a method, but the חכמים chose not to publicize it.

steps.title: What was the hidden method?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יצחק meant by 'there was another option.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'there was yet another option'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the details of the method רבי יצחק mentioned. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק only said that a method exists. The גמרא now wants to know exactly what it is.

phrases.english: What is 'there was yet another option'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an explanation of רבי יצחק's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The content of the hidden method.

steps.title: Carry it in steps of less than four cubits
steps.stepSummary: The method is to move the pouch in short stretches, each less than four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He carries it less than four cubits at a time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reveals the method: the person carries the pouch himself, but stops before each four אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה prohibition is carrying four אמות in a רשות הרבים in one move. By stopping before each four אמות, he never completes a full act of carrying. So he does not break the תורה law.

keyTerms.meaning: Each time less than four cubits

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean carrying is allowed in a normal way. Each short stretch must stop before four אמות, and that is exactly why the method is risky.

phrases.english: He carries it in stretches of less than four cubits each.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers what the hidden method is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Carrying the pouch in increments, each less than four אמות.

steps.title: Why did the חכמים hide it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חכמים chose not to reveal this method.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did the חכמים not want to reveal it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason the method was kept secret. This sets up the answer from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the method is permitted, it seems strange to hide it. The גמרא wants to know the reason.

phrases.english: Why did the Sages not want to reveal it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After learning the method, the גמרא asks why it was hidden.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for concealing the method.

steps.title: Because of the verse about concealing for God's honor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes משלי: it is God's honor to conceal a matter, and the honor of kings to search out a matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the verse: 'It is the honor of God to conceal a matter, and the honor of kings to search out a matter.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that teaches that some things should be hidden for the sake of כבוד שמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says that sometimes keeping something hidden honors God. The גמרא applies this to the method of carrying in short stretches. But it is not yet clear how God's honor is involved here, which leads to the next question.

phrases.english: Because of: 'It is the honor of God to conceal a matter,'
'and the honor of kings to search out a matter.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why the method was hidden.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in משלי teaches that concealing certain matters is God's honor.

steps.title: How is God's honor involved here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: what honor of God is involved in hiding a method of carrying?
steps.simpleTranslation: And here, what 'honor of God' is there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the use of the פסוק. It is not clear how hiding a carrying method has anything to do with God's honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to be about hiding deep or holy matters. A practical שבת technique does not obviously fit. The גמרא demands a concrete connection.

phrases.english: And here, what 'honor of God' is there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the פסוק applies to this case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The application of 'כבוד אלהים הסתר דבר' to the method of carrying less than four אמות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק speaks of God's honor, and no such honor seems to be at stake in a practical carrying method.

steps.title: The concern: he may carry a full four cubits
steps.stepSummary: The answer: if people knew this method, they might end up carrying a full four אמות in a רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he will come to carry four cubits in the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the method was hidden to protect people from accidentally breaking a תורה law of שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying in short stretches is risky, because a person can easily forget to stop and go a full four אמות. Protecting people from a תורה violation of שבת is the 'honor of God' that hiding the method preserves.
steps.whatToRemember: Carrying less than four אמות at a time technically avoids the Torah prohibition. The חכמים still hid this method, because a person might slip and carry a full four אמות in a רשות הרבים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: the חכמים sometimes do not publicize a technical leniency when spreading it could lead people into a real איסור.

phrases.english: Perhaps he will come to carry
four cubits in the public domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּילְמָא אָתֵי לְאֵתוֹיֵי אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by naming the danger that hiding the method prevents.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a preventive concern (גזירה-style worry) as the 'honor of God'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No honor of God is connected to hiding a carrying technique.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hiding it prevents people from slipping into carrying four אמות in a רשות הרבים, which protects God's honor.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע disagree about the eighteen decrees
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a dispute about the day the eighteen גזירות were made. רבי אליעזר says they 'heaped the measure,' meaning they did well. רבי יהושע says they 'leveled the measure,' meaning they did harm.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר says, on that day they heaped up the סאה. רבי יהושע says, on that day they leveled off the סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The rule of handing the pouch to a גוי was one of the eighteen גזירות made on one famous day. Here the גמרא brings a ברייתא where two תנאים argue over whether that day was good or bad.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture a measuring cup called a סאה. רבי אליעזר says the חכמים 'heaped it up': they added fences that protect the תורה. רבי יהושע says they 'leveled it off': too many גזירות make the people's load too heavy, and then they drop even real תורה laws.

keyTerms.meaning: On that very day (when the eighteen גזירות were made)
They heaped up (filled past the top)
They leveled off (wiped the top flat)
A measuring vessel or unit of volume

steps.confusionAlert: Both images use the same measuring cup. 'Heaping' is the positive picture (more protection). 'Leveling' is the negative picture (taking away, because people will fail to keep the laws).
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that adding rabbinic fences is not automatically good. A fence that is too hard to keep can backfire.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
On that day they heaped up the se'ah measure.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
On that day they leveled off the se'ah measure.
phrases.notes: Meaning they took away, because too many decrees cause people to fail.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם גָּדְשׁוּ סְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining why the short-stretch method was hidden, the גמרא widens the view to the eighteen גזירות, which include the rule of handing the pouch to a גוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a תנאים dispute over whether the eighteen גזירות strengthened observance or overloaded it.

steps.title: The parable for רבי אליעזר's view: a basket that still holds mustard
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives a parable for רבי אליעזר. A basket full of large squash and gourds still has room for tiny mustard seeds. In the same way, the eighteen גזירות fit in and last.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: the parable of רבי אליעזר. What is this like? Like a basket full of cucumbers and gourds. A person puts mustard seed into it, and it holds it.
steps.whatsHappening: A second ברייתא gives a picture to explain רבי אליעזר's positive view of the eighteen גזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Big vegetables leave gaps, and tiny mustard seeds slip into those gaps without pushing anything out. Likewise, the new גזירות fit among the תורה's laws without harming them. They only add protection.

keyTerms.meaning: To what is the matter similar?

phrases.english: It was taught: the parable of Rabbi Eliezer:
To what is the matter similar?
To a basket full of cucumbers and gourds,
a person puts mustard seed into it,
and it holds it.
phrases.notes: The gaps absorb the small seeds. Nothing is lost.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: מָשָׁל דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates רבי אליעזר's side of the dispute in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גזירות fit in and are retained, like small seeds in a basket of large vegetables.

steps.title: The parable for רבי יהושע's view: a bowl of honey that overflows
steps.stepSummary: The parable for רבי יהושע: a bowl already full of honey overflows when pomegranates and nuts are added. In the same way, extra גזירות push out real תורה laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: The parable of רבי יהושע. What is this like? Like a bowl full of honey. One puts pomegranates and nuts into it, and it spills out.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the opposite picture, explaining רבי יהושע's negative view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Honey fills every gap, so anything added forces honey out over the edge. Likewise, the people's capacity is already full with תורה laws. Adding heavy גזירות makes them 'spill out' even real איסורים.

keyTerms.meaning: A large bowl or kneading trough

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: the גזירות fit in and protect, like a basket that still holds mustard. רבי יהושע: the גזירות overload and push out תורה law, like a bowl of honey that overflows.

phrases.aramaic: מָשָׁל דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה —
phrases.english: The parable of Rabbi Yehoshua: to what is the matter similar?
To a bowl full of honey,
one puts pomegranates and nuts into it,
and it spills out.
phrases.notes: The honey (the original תורה law) is lost.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָשָׁל דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting parable to step 14, completing the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Extra גזירות cause people to lose even what they already had, like honey spilling from a full bowl.

steps.title: Isn't placing the pouch on the donkey forbidden as driving a loaded animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה: if no גוי is present, one puts the pouch on his donkey. It challenges this, because leading a loaded animal on שבת (מחמר) is forbidden by the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The master said: if there is no גוי with him, he places it on the donkey. But isn't he then leading a loaded animal? And the תורה said, 'You shall not do any work'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's next rule and quotes it. It then immediately attacks it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse 'לא תעשה כל מלאכה... ובהמתך' forbids having your animal do מלאכה for you on שבת. Walking behind a loaded animal and driving it is called מחמר. So how can the משנה allow loading the pouch onto the donkey?

keyTerms.meaning: The master said (quoting an earlier source, here the משנה)
Driving or leading a loaded animal
The Merciful One (that is, the תורה)
You shall not do any work (the verse that includes one's animal)

steps.confusionAlert: The problem here is not that the person himself carries. The problem is that his animal is doing the carrying on שבת, which the תורה also forbids.

phrases.english: The master said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין עִמּוֹ גּוֹי מַנִּיחוֹ עַל הַחֲמוֹר.
phrases.english: If there is no gentile with him, he places it on the donkey.
But isn't he driving a loaded animal?
And the Torah said, "You shall not do any work"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר אֵין עִמּוֹ גּוֹי מַנִּיחוֹ עַל הַחֲמוֹר. וַהֲלֹא מְחַמֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion of the eighteen גזירות and returns to analyzing the משנה's rules.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that one may place the pouch on the donkey.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Loading one's animal and driving it is the forbidden act of מחמר, derived from the verse that includes one's animal in the שבת prohibition.

steps.title: Place it on the donkey while it is already walking
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה answers that one places the pouch on the donkey while it is moving. Then the donkey never lifts the object from a resting position, so there is no full act of carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: he places it on her while she is walking.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה defends the משנה by limiting how the pouch is placed on the donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full תורה violation of carrying needs עקירה (lifting from a place) and הנחה (setting down in a place). If the donkey is already walking when the pouch goes on, the donkey never 'lifted' it from rest. So the act is not a complete מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the answer
He places it on her (the donkey)

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
He places it on her while she is walking.
phrases.notes: So the donkey performs no עקירה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: מַנִּיחוֹ עָלֶיהָ כְּשֶׁהִיא מְהַלֶּכֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מחמר challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (the specific manner of loading)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Loading the donkey is always full מחמר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Loading it while it walks avoids עקירה, so there is no complete מלאכה.

steps.title: But the donkey will have to stop at some point
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the donkey is bound to stop to urinate or relieve itself. When it stops and then starts again, there is a full עקירה and הנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is impossible that she won't stop to urinate or to drop dung, and then there is lifting and setting down!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in רב אדא בר אהבה's answer by pointing to something that will naturally happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the donkey started out walking, at some point it will stand still. That stop counts as an הנחה. When it starts walking again, that is a new עקירה. So the full forbidden act returns.

keyTerms.meaning: Lifting an object from its place (the start of carrying)
Setting an object down (the end of carrying)

phrases.english: But it is impossible that she will not stop
to urinate or to drop dung,
and then there is lifting and setting down!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אִי אֶפְשָׁר דְּלָא קָיְימָא לְהַשְׁתִּין מַיִם וּלְהַטִּיל גְּלָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's claim that loading the donkey while it walks avoids a full מלאכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The donkey's natural stops create a new הנחה, and its restart creates a new עקירה.

steps.title: Remove the pouch whenever the donkey stops
steps.stepSummary: The answer: he puts the pouch on only while the donkey walks, and takes it off whenever the donkey stands still. That way there is never an עקירה or הנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When she walks, he places it on her. When she stands, he takes it off her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem from step 18 with a practical procedure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pouch is never on the donkey while the donkey is at rest. So the donkey never sets it down and never lifts it up. The method from step 17 still works.

phrases.english: When she is walking, he places it on her;
when she stands, he takes it off her.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהִיא מְהַלֶּכֶת מַנִּיחוֹ עָלֶיהָ, כְּשֶׁהִיא עוֹמֶדֶת נוֹטְלוֹ הֵימֶנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical procedure that avoids the problem
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every stop of the donkey creates עקירה and הנחה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Removing the pouch at each stop prevents any עקירה or הנחה.

steps.title: If so, he could use a fellow Jew the same way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if this method avoids any עקירה and הנחה, then he could also place the pouch on a fellow Jew while that Jew walks. Why does the משנה prefer the donkey?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even his friend as well!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer by showing it seems to prove too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If placing the object only while the carrier is moving, and removing it when he stops, avoids מלאכה, the same should work with a fellow Jew. Yet the משנה lists the donkey as the option when there is no גוי, not a fellow Jew. This suggests the answer is missing something.
steps.confusionAlert: This is a challenge, not a ruling. The גמרא is not permitting the use of a fellow Jew. It is asking why the משנה did not suggest it if the method really works.

phrases.english: If so, even his fellow as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the procedure from step 19 by extending its logic.
steps.kashyaTarget: The method of loading only while walking and unloading when stopping.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same method should then allow placing the pouch on a fellow Jew, yet the משנה only mentions the donkey.

steps.title: רב פפא's three-level scale: yourself, your fellow, your donkey
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers why the donkey is better than a fellow Jew. Whatever would bring a חטאת if done yourself is exempt but forbidden through a fellow Jew. Whatever is exempt but forbidden through a fellow Jew is fully permitted through your donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Anything that would make a person liable to bring a sin-offering if he did it with his own body is exempt but forbidden if he does it through his fellow. Anything that is exempt but forbidden through his fellow is permitted from the outset through his donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 20: why does the משנה prefer the donkey over a fellow Jew? רב פפא gives a ladder of three levels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting the pouch on a walking fellow Jew avoids a full תורה violation, but it counts as two people doing one מלאכה together, which is forbidden מדרבנן. With a donkey, רב פפא rules it is permitted from the outset. So the same trick that is only 'exempt but forbidden' with a person becomes fully permitted with a donkey.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin-offering brought for violating שבת by mistake
Exempt from punishment, but still forbidden
With his own body, doing it himself

steps.whatToRemember: Three levels: yourself = חטאת; through a fellow Jew = פטור אבל אסור; through your donkey (with the walking trick) = מותר לכתחילה.
steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not saying that driving a loaded donkey is always permitted. He is talking about the special method from Steps 17-19, where the pouch is put on and taken off only while the donkey is moving. That method has no עקירה or הנחה.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Anything for which, done with his own body, one is liable a sin-offering —
through his fellow, he is exempt but it is forbidden;
anything that through his fellow is exempt but forbidden —
through his donkey is permitted from the outset.
phrases.notes: This is why the משנה chose the donkey.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כׇּל שֶׁבְּגוּפוֹ חַיָּיב חַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Graded scale of severity between a person and an animal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the walking method avoids עקירה and הנחה, a fellow Jew should work just as well as a donkey.
steps.terutzMaskana: With a fellow Jew it is still forbidden (פטור אבל אסור). With a donkey it is fully permitted, so the donkey is preferred.

steps.title: Running home with a package on one's shoulder
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה rules that if שבת begins while one's package is on his shoulder, he may run home under it. The גמרא infers that only running is allowed, not walking slowly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: If his package was resting on his shoulder, he runs beneath it until he reaches his home. Specifically running; but walking little by little, no.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching about the same situation: a person caught by nightfall while carrying a package. He may run home with it, but he may not stroll.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The package was already on his shoulder before שבת, so he never lifted it on שבת. Running is allowed as long as he keeps moving, while walking slowly is forbidden. The reason comes in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:

phrases.aramaic: הָיְתָה חֲבִילָתוֹ מוּנַּחַת לוֹ עַל כְּתֵיפוֹ —
phrases.english: If his package was resting on his shoulder —
he runs beneath it until he reaches his home.
Specifically running;
phrases.notes: The גמרא infers this from the wording.

phrases.english: but little by little — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: הָיְתָה חֲבִילָתוֹ מוּנַּחַת לוֹ עַל כְּתֵיפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New related ruling about carrying when nightfall arrives
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may run home with a package already on his shoulder, but may not walk slowly.

steps.title: Why only running?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason that running is allowed but slow walking is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slow walking seems no worse than running, since in both cases he never lifts the package on שבת. So the difference needs a reason.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind Step 22
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why running is permitted but slow walking is forbidden

steps.title: Running acts as a reminder
steps.stepSummary: Without a noticeable change, he may forget it is שבת, stop to rest, and do a real עקירה and הנחה. Running is the reminder.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he has no reminder, he may come to do a lifting and a placing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: running is an unusual way to move, so it reminds him that it is שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he walks normally, nothing feels different, so he might stop to rest and then start again. That would be a full עקירה and הנחה. Running keeps him alert and stops him from pausing.

keyTerms.meaning: Lifting an object from rest and putting it down, the two parts of carrying

phrases.english: Since he has no noticeable reminder,
he may come to do a lifting and a placing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 23
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Running serves as a היכירא, so he will not stop and create an עקירה and הנחה.

steps.title: He must stop when he arrives home
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: when he reaches home he will have to stop for a moment, which means he carried from רשות הרבים into רשות היחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ultimately, when he reaches his home, it is impossible that he will not stand for a bit, and he brings it in from the public domain to the private domain!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אדא's ruling: running does not solve the problem at the end of the trip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if he never stops on the way, arriving home brings him to a halt. That stop completes a move from רשות הרבים to רשות היחיד, which looks like a תורה-level act of carrying.

phrases.english: Ultimately, when he reaches his home,
it is impossible that he will not stand still a bit,
and he is bringing it in from the public domain to the private domain!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אדא's ruling from Step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's permission to run home with the package
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Arrival at home forces a stop, and that stop completes an act of carrying into רשות היחיד.

steps.title: He throws the package in an unusual way
steps.stepSummary: The answer: when he gets home, he throws the package down in an unusual manner, so the הנחה is not a normal תורה-level act.
steps.simpleTranslation: He throws it in an unusual manner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אדא: he does not set the package down normally when he arrives. He tosses it off in an unusual way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מלאכה done כלאחר יד, in an unusual manner, is not a תורה violation. So the final placing inside the house is not a real הנחה. The ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: In an unusual manner, literally 'with the back of the hand'

phrases.english: He throws it in an unusual manner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the final act is done כלאחר יד
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The stop at home is a normal הנחה, a תורה violation.
steps.terutzMaskana: He throws the package off in an unusual way, so there is no תורה-level הנחה.
steps.whatToRemember: Running home is allowed because it reminds him not to stop. The final drop at home is done כלאחר יד, so it is not a תורה violation.

steps.title: Driving a loaded animal brings full liability
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא rules that one who drives his loaded animal on שבת brings a חטאת if he did it by mistake, and is liable to סקילה if he did it on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: One who drives behind his animal on שבת — if unintentionally, he is liable a חטאת; if intentionally, he is liable סקילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about מחמר, leading a loaded animal on שבת. It connects back to the donkey discussion in Step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא treats driving a loaded animal like doing the מלאכה yourself. That is the most severe level. This is the regular case of driving, with full עקירה and הנחה, not the special walking method of Steps 17-19.

keyTerms.meaning: One who drives or leads a loaded animal

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with רב פפא's 'permitted with the donkey' in Step 21. רב פפא's case uses the special method that has no עקירה or הנחה. רמי בר חמא is talking about ordinary driving of a loaded animal.

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said:
One who drives behind his animal on Shabbat,
if unintentionally — he is liable a sin-offering;
if intentionally — he is liable stoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: הַמְחַמֵּר אַחֵר בְּהֶמְתּוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the topic of מחמר raised in Step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Driving a loaded animal on שבת carries full liability: חטאת if by mistake, סקילה if on purpose.

steps.title: What is the source for this severity?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why driving an animal should be as severe as doing the מלאכה yourself.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רמי בר חמא's ruling, setting up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal does the carrying, not the person. So it is surprising that the person gets the full punishment. The גמרא wants a source.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of Step 27
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for full liability when driving an animal

steps.title: רבא: 'You and your animal' are compared
steps.stepSummary: רבא derives it from the פסוק 'לא תעשה כל מלאכה אתה ובהמתך'. The animal is compared to the person, so the punishments are the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Because the verse says: 'You shall not do any work, you and your animal.' His animal is like himself: just as for himself, unintentionally he brings a sin-offering and intentionally he is stoned, so too with his animal, unintentionally he brings a sin-offering and intentionally he is stoned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question with a פסוק. Because the תורה puts 'you' and 'your animal' in the same phrase, the animal's work is treated like your own work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words אתה ובהמתך link the person and his animal into one rule. So the penalties for the person's own מלאכה, חטאת and סקילה, carry over to work done through his animal. This is the source for רמי בר חמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as ... so too (a comparison formula)

steps.whatToRemember: רמי בר חמא's full liability for מחמר comes from רבא's reading of 'אתה ובהמתך': your animal is compared to you.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next challenges in the sugya. Treating מחמר as a full Torah violation with סקילה is a strong claim, and the גמרא will go on to test it.

phrases.english: Rava said: Because the verse says:
"You shall not do any work,
you and your animal" —
his animal is similar to himself:
just as he — unintentionally is liable a sin-offering,
intentionally is liable stoning;
so too with his animal —
unintentionally he is liable a sin-offering,
intentionally he is liable stoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 28
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'אתה ובהמתך' compares the animal to the person, so the person has the same liability for the animal's work.

steps.title: רבא's first refutation: the whole Torah is compared to idolatry
steps.stepSummary: רבא says there are two refutations of רמי בר חמא's ruling. The first is a היקש: the פסוק links the whole Torah to עבודה זרה. Since עבודה זרה requires an act done with one's own body, so does שבת. Driving an animal is not such an act.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There are two refutations of this statement. First, it is written: 'One law shall you have for one who acts by mistake... and the soul that acts with a high hand.' The whole Torah is compared to עבודה זרה. Just as עבודה זרה is a case where he does an action with his own body, here too he is only liable once he does an action with his own body.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now attacks רמי בר חמא's ruling from the previous steps. He says it can be refuted in two ways, and here he gives the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These פסוקים speak about a person who serves עבודה זרה by mistake. Because the פסוק says 'one law', the entire תורה is linked to עבודה זרה, which is only punished when the person himself does the act. So on שבת, too, a קרבן חטאת or סקילה requires a physical act by the person, not by his animal.

keyTerms.meaning: There are two refutations of this statement
With a high hand, meaning deliberately and defiantly
Was compared (a היקש, linking two topics through a פסוק)
An action done with his own body

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying driving an animal on שבת is permitted. He is only saying it does not carry the severe punishments of חטאת or סקילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general principle: the severe punishments for תורה prohibitions require a direct physical act by the person himself.

phrases.english: Rava said: there are two refutations of this matter:
One, as it is written:
"One law shall there be for you
for one who acts by mistake
and the soul that acts with a high hand" —
phrases.notes: Numbers 15:29–30, a passage about idol worship

phrases.aramaic: הוּקְּשָׁה כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה:
phrases.english: the entire Torah is compared to idol worship:

phrases.aramaic: מָה עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה דְּעָבֵיד מַעֲשֶׂה בְּגוּפֵיהּ,
phrases.english: just as idol worship is where he does an action with his own body,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי עַד דְּעָבֵיד מַעֲשֶׂה בְּגוּפֵיהּ.
phrases.english: here too, he is not liable until he does an action with his own body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רמי בר חמא's ruling (step 27) and the derivation that the animal is treated like the person (step 29).
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's ruling that driving a loaded animal brings חטאת or סקילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A היקש to עבודה זרה requires a bodily act for these punishments. Driving an animal is not a bodily act by the person.

steps.title: רבא's second refutation: an inference from the משנה about stoning
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes the משנה listing those who get סקילה: one who violates שבת with an act that brings חטאת by mistake and סקילה on purpose. The wording implies there is some שבת prohibition with neither punishment. He suggests this is driving an animal (מחמר).
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, we learned in a משנה: 'One who violates שבת with a thing for which one is liable to a חטאת if done by mistake, and to סקילה if done on purpose.' This implies there is something for which one is not liable to a חטאת by mistake, nor to סקילה on purpose. And what is it? Is it not the prohibition of driving an animal?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his second argument. He reads the משנה's careful wording to show there is a שבת prohibition without these punishments, and suggests it is driving an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה could have just said 'one who violates שבת'. Instead it added a qualifier, which implies some violations of שבת do not carry חטאת or סקילה. רבא proposes that the excluded case is מחמר, which would directly contradict רמי בר חמא.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, introducing an additional argument
One who drives a loaded donkey or animal

phrases.english: And furthermore, we learned in a mishna:
One who violates Shabbat with a matter
for which one is liable to a sin-offering if done by mistake
and to stoning if done on purpose.
This implies that there is something
for which one is not liable to a sin-offering if done by mistake
nor to stoning if done on purpose,
and what is it? Is it not [the prohibition of] driving an animal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא's second of the two promised refutations.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's ruling that מחמר is punishable by סקילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's qualifier implies a שבת prohibition with no חטאת or סקילה, and the natural candidate is מחמר.

steps.title: Rejecting the second refutation: the משנה may mean תחומין or הבערה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's second argument. The case the משנה excludes might be תחומין according to רבי עקיבא, or הבערה according to רבי יוסי, not מחמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It could be תחומין, according to רבי עקיבא, and הבערה, according to רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's second proof. It offers other prohibitions that could explain the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that תחומין is a תורה prohibition but carries no חטאת or סקילה. רבי יוסי holds that lighting a fire on שבת is punished with מלקות, not סקילה. Either one can be the case the משנה excludes, so the משנה is no proof about מחמר.

keyTerms.meaning: The boundaries for walking outside the city on שבת
A תנא who holds תחומין is a Torah prohibition
A תנא who holds הבערה is only a לאו, punished with מלקות

steps.whatToRemember: רבא refuted רמי בר חמא in two ways. The second, from the משנה's wording, was rejected because the משנה could mean תחומין or הבערה. The first, the היקש to עבודה זרה, still stands.
steps.confusionAlert: Only the second refutation is rejected here. The first one (the comparison to עבודה זרה) is not answered.

phrases.english: No,
[it means] Shabbat boundaries, according to Rabbi Akiva,
and kindling, according to Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn from the משנה in step 31.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רבא's second refutation (the inference from the משנה), not the first.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference does not have to point to מחמר. Other prohibitions without חטאת or סקילה, such as תחומין or הבערה, can be what the משנה excludes.
